summary: The paper introduces a single-location regression (SLR) model as a controlled testbed to compare softmax vs. linear (and other) attention activations, and combines classical population-risk analysis with a high-dimensional replica-based characterization of the ERM. The main results — softmax attains Bayes risk under the SLR/max-SLR settings while linear attention has a provable gap that widens with variable sequence length — are clean, and the finite-sample extension via replica equations agrees with numerical optimization. The contribution is theoretical, narrow in scope (no query, single-token dependency, no depth, essentially one head), and partially overlapping with concurrent work (Dragutinović et al. 2025; Barnfield et al. 2026; [Author] et al. 2025), but it provides a principled, cleanly-scoped explanation of a widely-cited empirical phenomenon and is well-executed within its regime.
strengths: Clear formalization: SLR unifies spiked-SLR and max-SLR via a weight function gν, and the framework is expressive enough to compare softmax, linear, elementwise-erf, and softplus-kernelized attention within one analysis.

The Bayes-optimality of softmax under the stated symmetry condition on gν (Prop. 4.2, Nishimori-type identity) is a compact, sharp statement that isolates *why* softmax is well-specified here, and the paired negative result for linear attention (Cor. 4.3–4.4) directly implicates the missing normalization as the failure mode.

The finite-sample analysis (Result 5.1) extends sequence multi-index replica machinery to variable L and general gν and reduces the ERM risk to a small system of self-consistent equations, whose predictions match a quasi-Newton solver on the actual empirical risk (Fig. 3).

Ablations across activations (linear vs. erf vs. normalized softplus vs. softmax) and across sequence-length distributions (L=2 vs. L∼Unif{1,2,3} vs. L=10) cleanly separate the roles of nonlinearity growth rate and cross-token normalization.
Limitations (no query vector, manifold restriction, replica non-rigor, absence of a formal landscape argument) are stated rather than hidden.

key_concerns.issue: Novelty relative to closely related concurrent/prior work is not sufficiently delineated. Marion et al. (2025) / [Author] et al. (2025) already study a spiked SLR-like model, Troiani et al. (2025) supplies the sequence two-index Bayes-optimal analysis, and Dragutinović et al. (2025) is explicitly cited as concurrently arguing softmax > linear via different techniques. The paper claims generalization via variable L, weighting gν, and renormalization enabling softmax analysis, but there is no side-by-side statement of what is new theorem-by-theorem versus these works.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a compact table or paragraph in Section 2 that maps each formal contribution (Prop 4.1/4.2/4.3/4.4, Cor 4.3/4.4, Result 5.1) to its closest prior/concurrent counterpart and highlights the delta (variable L, gν, softmax handled, replica for two-index with weight).

key_concerns.issue: The manifold assumption (mkv=mvk=qvk=0) is central: all closed-form comparisons and Result 5.1 are stated on this manifold, and the paper concedes that other local minima exist off the manifold and that a formal proof is 'delicate'. This is a load-bearing simplification that partially blunts the 'softmax outperforms linear' claim for GD/SGD-trained models.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide a quantitative empirical check at finite D: initialize off-manifold and track (mkv, mvk, qvk) along GD, and/or run seeds where random init lands measurably off M. Report the fraction of runs that converge to on-manifold minima and any observed off-manifold minima's risk relative to the on-manifold one.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical reporting for the finite-sample experiments (Fig. 3) is thin as described in the body: N,D=1e4, regularizers grid-searched, but there is no mention of number of seeds, confidence intervals, or variance across problem draws (k*, v*, dataset). The core claim of Section 5 is that a random quantity concentrates on Eσ(α); showing that concentration numerically requires seed-level dispersion.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± std over multiple seeds for the quasi-Newton runs in Fig. 3, and include a supplementary figure demonstrating the concentration of the ERM test risk around Eσ(α) as D grows.

key_concerns.issue: The framing motivates the work via retrieval-vs-language behavior of real LLMs (Fig. 1 borrowed from Shen et al. 2024), but the SLR setup abstracts away nearly all of what makes real retrieval hard: no query vector, one relevant token, single head/layer, Gaussian tokens, D→∞. The paper does not empirically bridge back — e.g., a small transformer trained on an SLR-like sequence task where softmax vs. linear-attention parity/gap is measured against Result 5.1's predictions.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a small controlled experiment training a 1–2 layer transformer with softmax vs. linear attention on a synthetic retrieval task instantiating SLR/max-SLR, and check qualitative agreement (gap widening with L, ν) with the theory. Even a modest experiment would substantially strengthen the significance claim.

key_concerns.issue: The kernelized-attention comparison (softplus) is used to argue that a kernel must grow fast enough to dominate irrelevant tokens, but the discussion is limited to one kernel choice. Since 'kernelized attention' is the main practical linear-time alternative, more than one ϕ (e.g., ELU+1 as in Performer/Katharopoulos, cos² as cited) would strengthen the claim.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one additional kernel ϕ (e.g., positive-orthogonal features à la Performer or ELU+1) to Fig. 2 for spiked-SLR and max-SLR.

key_concerns.issue: Result 5.1 is stated as a 'result' (non-rigorous replica prediction). The paper says a proof via the replicon condition is left to future work. For a theoretical paper whose Section 5 is a headline contribution, some rigorous corroboration (e.g., a matching upper/lower bound in a special case, or a proved concentration lemma) would substantially raise the bar.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Prove at least one rigorous corollary of Result 5.1 in a tractable special case (e.g., linear attention, deterministic L, ν=0), and clearly delineate what is rigorous vs. replica-heuristic.

key_concerns.issue: Some notation and typesetting are hard to parse (the free-floating variables and stray sub/superscripts around eqns. (5), (12)–(13), (17)–(25) read as extraction artifacts), which makes it hard for a reviewer to verify the equations independently.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Polish the final display equations; ensure every symbol is defined at first use in the body (e.g., cν, cL, χ ℓ, γ ℓ, ω ℓ, χ′, z′).

questions_for_authors: How does your setting differ mathematically, theorem-by-theorem, from Marion et al. (2025), Troiani et al. (2025), and Dragutinović et al. (2025)? A precise attribution would help calibrate novelty.
How sensitive is the finite-D quasi-Newton agreement with Result 5.1 to initialization? Do random inits ever land at off-manifold minima with materially different Eσ, and if so, how often?
For max-SLR at finite ν, does softmax still achieve Bayes risk, or only in the ν→∞ / spiked limits considered? The condition (6) suggests only certain gν yield Nishimori — please clarify the scope.
In Section 5, how many seeds underlie Fig. 3, and what is the empirical variance of Eσ(k̂,v̂) at N,D=1e4? Does concentration on Eσ(α) tighten predictably as D grows?

Can you validate the theory on a small trained transformer (softmax vs. linear-attention head) on a synthetic dataset instantiating spiked-SLR or max-SLR, and check whether the qualitative gap trends with L and ν match the predictions?

For the kernelized comparison, would other kernels (Performer-style positive random features, ELU+1) close the gap to softmax, or is the growth-rate criterion you highlight the fundamental obstruction?

The 'we argue this captures one-pass SGD performance' claim (Sec. 4) is important but not proved. Is there a more precise statement (e.g., matching upper bounds on the sample complexity of one-pass SGD along the lines of Ben Arous et al. 2021) you can offer?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly appropriately scoped — the paper is careful to label Result 5.1 as replica-based and to acknowledge the manifold assumption and simplified setting — but the framing in the abstract ('softmax consistently outperforms linear attention') is broader than the proven regime, and some corollaries (Cor. 4.3–4.4) are stated in specific asymptotic limits that should be surfaced more clearly at claim time.

significance.justification: Provides a principled, sharp explanation of a widely-observed empirical phenomenon (softmax's edge on retrieval-like tasks) within a controlled model — modestly impactful for the theory subcommunity, less so beyond because the setting abstracts away query vectors, depth, and realistic tokenization.

novelty.justification: Genuine but incremental: variable-length sequences, generic gν, and replica analysis of softmax nonlinearity extend prior sequence multi-index work, but concurrent papers (Dragutinović et al. 2025; Marion et al. 2025; Troiani et al. 2025) cover overlapping ground and the delta is not crisply delineated.

rigor.justification: The population-risk propositions look correct (Nishimori-style argument is well-known and applied cleanly), and the replica derivation is standard for this literature; the manifold restriction and non-rigorous replica step are honestly flagged rather than swept aside.

statistical_soundness.justification: Numerical experiments illustrate the theory but the body does not describe seeds, error bars, or concentration checks for the ERM around Eσ(α); the main quantitative claim of Section 5 (concentration) is asserted rather than empirically probed.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations (no query, manifold assumption, replica non-rigor, restricted activation family, kernel choice) are stated openly; the abstract slightly overreaches in generality but the body scopes the claims to specific models and limits.

clarity.justification: Organization is standard and results are signposted, but the mathematical exposition is dense and several equation blocks are difficult to parse (partly extraction artifacts); a reader not already fluent in sequence multi-index / replica notation will struggle.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure with intro, related work, model, population analysis, finite-sample analysis, and pointers to appendices; length appears within norms and headings are appropriate.

reproducibility.justification: The data model, activation classes, order-parameter equations, and optimization procedure are described in enough detail to reimplement, and code is referenced; however hyperparameters, seeds, grid ranges, and quasi-Newton settings for Fig. 3 are only pointed to in appendices and not summarized in-body.

related_work.justification: Covers kernelized attention, SSMs, associative recall / MQAR, sequence multi-index literature, and Nishimori/statistical physics tools, and explicitly names concurrent works — though the delineation of contribution against those concurrents could be sharper.

figure_quality.justification: Judging from captions, Fig. 2 systematically compares four activations across two SLR variants and three L regimes and Fig. 3 overlays replica predictions with a solver's empirical ERM — both figures directly support the paper's central claims rather than decorate them.

breadth_generality.justification: The setup is deliberately narrow (one relevant token, no query vector, Gaussian tokens, one attention layer, D→∞), and generality claims relative to real transformer training are argued heuristically rather than tested with even a small trained-transformer experiment.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline accept: a clean, well-motivated theoretical contribution that formalizes a hypothesis about softmax's advantage and delivers matching population and finite-sample analyses; held back from clear accept by narrow scope, novelty overlap with concurrent work, replica-only Section 5, and thin statistical reporting.
